content: Repaired increment A mock-test gate DISAGREE. The two planned Pester selectors each run ten mock cases with zero failures, skips, or not-run cases; the real target gives one pass and nine missing-module failures. Callback wiring and policy metadata cases are materially improved. Three blocking gaps remain. Default callbacks do not verify workspace/TODO/binding/exact-policy request arguments, so wrong requests can receive canned good data. The slice-revision case makes its own callback choose the pinned revision and has no server-service pinning or binding-precedence proof; flow-a is not a BDPv4 fixture. Negative controls corrupt several fields together and use broad Should-Throw, so digest failure or an unrelated exception can mask broken graph/revision assertions. Production edits remain blocked until these test-oracle gaps are repaired and the mock gate is reviewed again.

failures.finding: Default resolve and fetch callbacks ignore requested workspace, TODO, bindingId, and policyId. A real adapter could request a wrong workspace or wrong exact policy ID and receive the same canned good reply, then pass every content assertion. This leaves the central exact-ID and scope contract unproven.
failures.evidence: Default callbacks return captured replies without checking any arguments
failures.remediation: Use strict spies for each case that record and reject wrong workspace/TODO/slice, bindingId and exact policyId; assert call counts and IDs, then rerun negative controls.

failures.finding: The active-slice pinning case programs the resolver callback itself to return revision 7 for slice-1 and revision 8 for slice-2. The adapter only forwards the callback result. It does not prove an authoritative service pins an existing slice or requires signed migration/new generation. The slice also has no binding-precedence case despite plan A, and the first graph is a flow-a proxy rather than a BDPv4 fixture.
failures.evidence: No backend process state or competing TODO/workspace/global bindings in New-Case
failures.remediation: Add server-service contract tests for binding precedence, pinned revision, unauthorized revision swap and signed migration/new generation. Use a BDPv4 manifest fixture and a distinct approved process fixture for slice A exit.

failures.finding: Oracle negative controls corrupt revision, graph, and digest together, then leave the digest wrong. Both Should-Throw checks can pass solely because the digest assertion works; graph and revision assertions may be broken. Broad Should-Throw also accepts unrelated exceptions.
failures.evidence: First wrong result has revision 6, GraphB and digest 0000; second fixes revision/graph but leaves digest 0000
failures.remediation: Use separate cases with exactly one bad field and valid companion fields, and assert the expected field-specific assertion failure rather than any exception.
